chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī ʿUbaydah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a woman sees purity while she is within the time of salat, then delays the ghusl until the time of another salat begins, then qada' of that salat which she neglected is upon her. And if she becomes pure during a prayer time, then delays the salat until the time of another salat begins, then she sees blood, then qada' of that salat which she neglected is upon her.

key_terms.دَمًا: blood indicating the return of bleeding
key_terms.فَرَّطَتْ: she neglected or fell short in performing the duty
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up an obligatory act after its time has passed
key_terms.وَقْتِ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the legally designated time for performing the prayer
key_terms.ٱلطُّهْرَ: ritual purity after the cessation of bleeding
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath required before resuming salat

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes pure during prayer time but delays ghusl or salat until the next prayer time, must she make up that prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who becomes pure from menstruation or similar bleeding during the time of salat. If she delays ghusl or the salat itself until the next prayer time enters, or until bleeding returns, she must perform the qada' of the prayer she neglected.
